1.explanation:
• audits/byte-efficiency/render-blocking-resources.js: the core audit implementation where protocol filtering is applied — this is where file:// URLs should be excluded but currently aren’t.  
• audits/byte-efficiency/render-blocking-resources-test.js: the unit tests that define expected behavior (which don’t cover file:// cases today); updating these tests will ensure we handle local resources correctly.  
• test-utils.js: provides helpers for constructing mock NetworkRecords in tests; you’ll need it to simulate file:// requests.  
• network-records-to-devtools-log.js & its test (network-records-to-devtools-log-test.js): transforms mock NetworkRecords into DevTools protocol format for the audit’s artifact pipeline; useful for reproducing how a file:// record gets fed into the audit.  
• create-test-trace.js: generates synthetic trace data used in the audit tests to build a synthetic “loading” environment.  
Together, these files cover the path from raw network/trace inputs through the render-blocking-resources audit logic, so you can write a failing test for file:// and then patch the audit to ignore those URLs.
1.bug_scenario: When auditing a page with Lighthouse (v8.1.0) via the CLI, any <file://>-sourced resource shows up under “Eliminate render-blocking resources” even though local (file:///) assets can’t actually block rendering. In the attached screenshot, Lighthouse flags file:///some/local/file as a blocking resource and reports ~0.59 s of savings, which is incorrect: local resources should be skipped by this audit.
